payload.description: Clamp effort on u_brown must never exceed its registry max_clamp_effort while grasped.

payload.explanation: u_brown final pose (0.40257,-0.15127,0.04341) vs placement frame (0.40352,-0.15192,0.04538): position delta ~2.26mm, within 10mm tolerance; orientation nearly identical quaternions, well within 10deg. No monitor fires during the step (clamp effort monitor and bystander monitors silent).

payload.description: Clamp effort on u_orange must never exceed its registry max_clamp_effort while grasped.
Previously seated u_brown must remain undisturbed while subsequent parts are handled.

payload.explanation: After the commanded descent to u_orange_placement, release and retreat, u_orange's queried pose was (0.5974,-0.2444,0.0388) with orientation far from the placement frame's (0.4030,-0.2470,0.0454); position delta ~23.5cm, orientation delta roughly 160deg (quaternion dot product near -0.26 after normalizing signs), both far outside tolerance. No monitor fired (clamp effort stayed in bounds and no in-hand-slip monitor was armed for this object, which is a monitoring gap I note here), so the departure was only caught by this place-step pose check. Camera view shows the part not seated on base1. Believed mechanism: the part was not rigidly seated/aligned at the commanded grasp-center target before release -- the move reported SUCCESS at the planner level but the part ended tipped and displaced, consistent with a collision/contact with u_brown or the fixture during descent, or the part slipping out of the jaws before or during release. I am reseating it as a new recovery step.

payload.description: Clamp effort on u_brown must never exceed its registry max_clamp_effort while grasped.
payload.detail: finger_joint effort exceeded max_clamp_effort while holding u_brown

payload.explanation: User commanded an abort mid-recovery. At the time of the abort, u_orange was still held in the gripper after a seat move had reported planner SUCCESS, but was not released/verified against u_orange_placement, and earlier queries during this same descent showed it already tipping (orientation drifting away from the intended square pose) partway through the slow descent. u_brown remains correctly seated and undisturbed. u_orange's true end-state is unresolved: still in the gripper, not seated, not released. The clamp-effort fire recorded earlier (mon_98b6b2602890, 106.068N attributed to u_brown) is judged a mis-armed-monitor artifact: it fired while u_orange (not u_brown) was the held object, since that monitor only reads finger_joint effort without checking held_object(); u_brown was already placed and released well before this timestamp, and 106N is also below u_orange's own 200N limit, so no real clamp-effort violation stands for either part. No bystander or fixture monitor fired; u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base1 and base2 all remained within their baselines throughout. Run is being stopped per explicit user instruction before u_orange's placement could be completed or verified.

Run stopped by explicit user abort instruction before the assembly was complete. u_brown was successfully seated at u_brown_placement within tolerance (position delta ~2.3mm, orientation ~0.3deg) and remained undisturbed for the rest of the run. u_orange's original place step failed badly (ended up ~23.5cm from its placement frame, tipped over) for reasons not fully diagnosed (believed slip or collision in transit); two recovery attempts to re-grasp and reseat it also ended in the part tipping/toppling after reaching the seat pose, and the motion backend also hit a run of transient CONTROL_FAILED errors (even on simple named-pose moves) during the second recovery, which recovered on retry. At the moment of abort, u_orange was still held in the gripper mid-descent on a third recovery attempt and had not been released, verified, or seated -- its true end-state is unresolved/incomplete, so this counts as a standing violation for u_orange's required effect. line_green and inverted_u_yellow were never reached. No bystander (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red) or fixture (base1, base2) monitor fired, and direct pose checks at the end confirm all of them remained at their baseline positions throughout -- the undisturbed-bystander and undisturbed-fixture requirements held for the whole run. One monitor fire occurred (clamp effort nominally attributed to u_brown, 106.068N vs its 100N limit) but is judged a mis-armed-monitor artifact: the monitor only read raw finger_joint effort without checking which object was actually held, and it fired while u_orange (limit 200N) was the held object and u_brown was already placed and released, so no real clamp-effort violation stands against either part's limit.
